'0.5 A scheme for labelling environment friendly products known as ECC-Mark bas been introduced at tbe instance of tbe Ministry of Environment and Forests (MEf), Government of India. The ECc-Mark sball be admimstered by tbe Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under lbe HIS Act, 1986 as per Ibe Resolution No. 71 dated 20 February 1991 and Resolution No. 425 dated 28 October 1992 publisbed in tbe Gazelle of the Government of India. For a product to be eligible for marking with the ECO-Mark il sball also carry the Standard Mark of BIS for quality besides meeting additional environment friendly (Ef) requirements. The environment friendly requirements for canned KUNDRI are, tberefore, included tbrough Amendment No. Ito tbis standard. 0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Insutuuon on 30th Apnl 1981. after the draft finalized by the Frurt-, and Vegetables Sectional Commrttee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products DIVISIon Councrl,

0.2 Canned KUNDRI IS the product prepared from mature KUNDRI of SUItable vaneties, The KUNDRI are cleaned and packed III brine They are processed In appropriate manner before and after being scaled In containers so as to prevent spoilage
0.2.1 KUNDRlls also called KUNDRU or TlNDORA

0.3 There IS ample scope for development of trade III canned KUNDRI. In order to ensure quality of the product It IS necessarv to have stuct quality control based on specifications. It was, therefore. felt necess,n y to tormulate an Indian Standard specificatron for the product 0.4 In the preparation of this standard, due consider.uron 11." been given to the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1Q54, the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules. 19';5 and the FrUIt Products Order, 1955. However, this standard" subject to the restnction unposed under these, wherever applicable
0.5 For the purpose 01 decidmg whether " partrcular requirement of this standard IS complied WIth, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysrs, shall be rounded off in accordance WIth IS: 2-1960 . The number of sigmficant places ret.nned m the rounded off value should be the same as that of tile specified value III this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 ThIS standard prescnbes the requirements for KUNDRI ( Coccinia cordifolia Cogn )

2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following defimtrons shall apply.
"Rules for roundmg off numerical values (reused)

IS : 9811 - 1981 2.1 Fill of Container - Expressed as water capacity of the container. The water capacity of the con tamer is the volume of distilled water at 20�C which the sealed container will hold when completely filled. 2.2 Drained Mass - The mass of the product obtained after cutting open the can and drainmg the product (see 7 of IS : 2860-1964� ). 2.3 Absence of Defects - The degree of freedom from extraneous material, such as stalk, yellow or pmkish hard seeds and also freedom from damage due to mechanical injury.

2.3.1 Blemished Units - Uruts that have some injury, such as worm hole, insect damage, physiological disorder; or other abnormality such as sun burn, scab, or enzyme activity on the surface, readily visrble to the naked eye to a noticeable degree Uneven drstrrbunon of pigment and change III colour normally associated with processing shall not be considered as defects. 2.3.2 Disintegrated Unit- The unit that has lost the normal shape or forms or from which portions have separated.
2.4 Can - Round open top sanitary Cans conforming to IS: 9396.1979t. 3. STYLES

3.1 KUNDRI used for canmng should have top and hottom end removed. They may have a logitudmal slit.
4. GRADES
4.1 Canned KUNDRI shall be of two grades, namely, Grade I and Grade 2.

5. REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Hygienic Requirements - The matenal shall be prepared and handled under strict hygienic condiuons (see 15: 6542-l972t ) by persons free from contagious and mfectious diseases and only in premises rnaintamed III a thoroughly clean and hygienic condition and having adequate and safe water supply. All workers shall use clean. white, washed clothing. Necessary precautions shall be taken to prevent mcidental contamination of the product from SOIled equipment or from personnel suffering from mjunes, 5.1.1 All equipment coming in contact wah raw materials or products in the course of manufacture shall be kept clean. An ample supply of steam and water, hose. brushes and other equipment necessary for proper cleaning

The covering bnne shall be practically clear, practically free from cloudiness and suspended matter and shall be practically free from discolouratron. b) Grade 2- The units shall be reasonably free from any defects which means that there shall not be present any extraneous matenals includmg stalk and there shall be present not more than four blemished uruts, not more than four dismtegrated units and not

PROCEDURE A-l.I Paonel of Judges - Scoring of the product shall be done by a panel of three to five judges. All the judges consutuung a panel shall be conversant with the factors governing the quahty of the product. The cans shall be opened and the contents poured separately into white porcelain bowls. Each judge shall mdependently examme the conterts from each of the cans and assign scores for different characterisncs. A-2.I.I The Judges shall consider the followmg charactenstrcs: Colour. texture and uniformny of SIze. taste and lJavour, and absence of defects.

A-l.3 System of Scoring - The vanations withm each factor are so descnbed that the scores may be ascertained for each factor and expressed numerically The relative Importance of each factor has been expressed numerically on a scale of 100. Each Judge shall give a score for the indiVIdual factors, by the method described III Table 3 and record his observations in the score sheet for mdivrdual judge.

A-l.2.1 The scores as number of P0InIS gtven on the score sheet by the judges for the contents of each can for the four factors shall be recorded lIT a tabular form In the score card and the average score calculated for each factor with overall average for each Can entered m the appropriate columns of the score card after complying with the condiuons specified in A-2.3.1 and A-2.3.2. A-2.3 Ascertaining the Score A-2.3.1 Agreement Among Judges ~ To ascertain the consistency of Judgement among the Judges, the total score assrgned by each of them for the contents of the same can shall be calculated by addrng up the score for the various md.vrdual characteristics. If the difference between the maximum and the rmrumum of tie total score 50 obtained does not exceed ( K + 5 ). where K IS the number of judges, the score shall be deemed as consrstent for the can under consideranon. If the difference exceeds ( K + 5), the most outlymg score. that is, the one whtch IS farthest from its immediate neighbour ( the scores being arranged in one order), shall be discarded and the consistency among the remaining Judges shall be examined. It

IS : 9811 - 1981

A-Z.3.Z When the consistency is thus established (A-J.3.1). the overall average scores given by the judges. whose scoring has been found to be consistent, shall be calculated for each can The average score for each of the individual characteristics shall also be calculated by taking into account the corresponding scores as given by the same Judges for the contents of the same can.
